title: Electronics Fundamentals Module 6: Microcontrollers, Soldering, Oscilloscopes & Serial Buses
overview: Covers ADC/DAC conversion, PWM, UART/I2C/SPI protocols, IPC soldering standards, and oscilloscope ground-clip safety.
art: MIXED-SIGNAL & PYTHON INTERFACE (?1)(?2)      SOLDER JOINT PROFILE (?3)
Analog Sensor ──► [ ADC ] ──► [ MCU / Pi ]         Good Joint    Cold Joint
[ Ground Clip] ───► Circuit GND ONLY! (Tied to AC Wall Earth Ground!)

1.label: ADC, DAC & PWM (Bridging Analog and Digital)
1.what: ADC (Analog-to-Digital Converter) turns real-world voltages (like temperature sensors) into binary numbers. PWM (Pulse Width Modulation) fakes analog output using fast digital pulses.
1.exam_facts: 10-bit ADC = 2^10 = 1,024 steps (0–1023). PWM Duty Cycle = (Time ON / Total Period) × 100%—used to dim LEDs or control DC motor speed efficiently without wasting heat.
1.troubleshoot: If an ADC reading is stuck at max (1023) or 0, check your sensor's ground reference and verify you didn't exceed the microcontroller's max input voltage (3.3V on Raspberry Pi/ESP32 vs 5V on Arduino Uno).

2.label: Serial Hardware Buses: UART, I2C & SPI
2.what: The three standard ways microcontrollers, sensors, and Python scripts (`pyserial` / `smbus`) talk to each other over wires.
2.exam_facts: UART (2 wires: TX->RX, RX<-TX, asynchronous, requires matching Baud rate like 9600/115200). I2C (2 wires: SDA data, SCL clock, supports 100+ addressed devices, needs pull-up resistors). SPI (4 wires: MOSI, MISO, SCLK, CS—fastest full-duplex).
2.troubleshoot: 90% of UART issues come from forgetting to cross TX to RX, forgetting a shared GND wire between devices, or mismatched baud rates (which prints garbled symbols).

3.label: IPC Soldering & Desoldering Standards
3.what: Joining components mechanically and electrically using melted solder alloy (60/40 or 63/37 Tin-Lead, or Lead-Free SAC305) and flux.
3.exam_facts: IPC-A-610 standard: A good through-hole joint has a smooth, shiny, concave fillet wetting both the pad and the lead. Flux removes oxidation so solder flows properly.
3.troubleshoot: A dull, grainy, ball-shaped 'cold solder joint' happens when the iron wasn't hot enough, the pad wasn't heated equally with the pin, or the part moved while cooling—reheat with fresh flux!

4.label: Oscilloscope Operation & Earth Ground Warning
4.what: Measures voltage over time so you can inspect waveforms, noise, ripple, and serial data pulses.
4.exam_facts: Key controls: Volts/Div (vertical amplitude), Seconds/Div (horizontal timebase), and Trigger (freezes a repeating waveform on screen). 10X probe setting reduces circuit loading and increases bandwidth.
4.troubleshoot: CRITICAL: The alligator ground clip on a bench oscilloscope is connected directly to Earth Ground through the wall plug! Clipping it onto a non-ground voltage point creates a dead short and can blow up your circuit or probe!
